description_ru: Мистер Браун обыскивает весь дом в поисках очков, разговаривает с пальто и ест сыр, а ответ оказывается совсем рядом.
text:
Mr. Brown is a quiet man with a big problem. He cannot find his glasses.

It is Monday morning. He wakes up at seven and reaches for the table next to his bed. His hand finds a book, a cup and an old sock. No glasses. The room looks like a soft grey cloud, because Mr. Brown cannot see well without them.

"Maybe they are in the kitchen," he says to himself.

He walks to the kitchen very slowly. On the way, he says good morning to a tall plant. The plant does not answer. Then he says sorry to a coat, because he thinks it is his wife. The coat does not answer either.

"Margaret?" he says. "Where are you? I need my glasses."

"I am in the bathroom," says his wife. "Why are you talking to the coat?"

"I am not talking to the coat," says Mr. Brown. "I am talking to... a friend."

Margaret laughs. "Look in the kitchen. You always read the newspaper there."

Mr. Brown goes into the kitchen and looks on the table. He sees a white thing and picks it up. It is soft and cold. He smells it. Cheese! It is a big piece of cheese, not a pair of glasses.

"Oh dear," he says. "This is not my glasses. This is my breakfast."

He eats the cheese, because he is hungry, and he continues the search. He looks in the fridge, behind the toaster, under the sofa and inside a shoe. In the shoe, he finds a very old biscuit, but he does not find the glasses.

Margaret comes into the kitchen with a towel on her head. "Still nothing?"

"Nothing. I look everywhere."

"Did you check the garden? Yesterday you read your book in the sun."

"The garden! Good idea."

Mr. Brown opens the back door and walks outside. The grass is wet, and his socks become wet too. He moves from chair to chair and feels every one with his hands. On the third chair, there is something hard. He picks it up with a smile, but it is only a flower pot.

Next door, Mrs. Taylor is watering her flowers. She watches him for a minute.

"Good morning, Mr. Brown! Are you okay?"

"Good morning, Mrs. Taylor. I am looking for my glasses. Please, can you help me?"

"Of course," says Mrs. Taylor. She puts down her water can and comes to the fence. She looks at his face for a long time. Then she looks at the sky. Then she looks at his face again.

"I think I know where they are," she says.

"Really? Where?"

"Well..." Mrs. Taylor stops. She is a polite woman and she does not want to laugh. "Why don't you go back to the kitchen and look in the mirror?"

"In the mirror? Why?"

"Please, just try it."

Mr. Brown goes back to the kitchen and walks to the little mirror on the wall. He stands very close, almost touching it. He sees a grey shape with two big ears and a funny hairstyle. Then he sees something shine on top of his head.

Slowly, he lifts his hand and touches the top of his hair. There they are! His glasses, sitting on his head like two little round birds.

"Margaret!" he shouts. "I found them! They are on my head!"

Margaret comes in again, still with the towel on her head. She sees the glasses and starts to laugh. She laughs so much that the towel falls on the floor.

"Don't laugh," says Mr. Brown. "It is not funny."

"It is a little funny," says Margaret. "You walk around the house for one hour with your glasses on your head, you talk to a coat, and you eat a cheese you cannot see."

"It is not funny," he says again, but now he is smiling too.

He puts the glasses on his nose. The world is clear again. He can see the kitchen, the sunny garden, the sleepy cat and his wife with the towel.

"Thank you for the idea of the mirror," he says to Mrs. Taylor in the garden. "Next time, I look there first."

"Next time, you only need to touch your head," she says.

That evening, Mr. Brown is very careful. He puts his glasses on the table next to the bed, right next to the cup and the book. Then he goes to sleep.

On Tuesday morning, he wakes up and puts them on at once. Then he looks around the room.

"Margaret," he says in a small voice. "I cannot find my phone."

Margaret looks at him for a long time. "Is it on your head?"

"No," he says, and he checks. "It is in my hand."

"Of course it is," says Margaret, and she laughs again.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Долгий «и», губы растянуты в улыбку; не сокращайте звук.
Кончик языка слегка между зубами, воздух выдыхайте мягко; не заменяйте на «с» или «з».
Начните с «а» и плавно перейдите в «и»; не разделяйте на два звука.
Короткий звук между «и» и «ы»; не растягивайте его как «ии».

questions.question: What does he eat by mistake?
Who tells him to look in the mirror?
